rubric: Write and test a program that meets these requirements.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
You do not need to declare any arrays, variables or constants; you may assume this has already been done.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

pc_cinema.title: Cinema seat bookings
pc_cinema.intro: A cinema screen has 10 rows of seats, with 20 seats in each row. The two-dimensional (2D) array Seats[1:10, 1:20] stores "E" for an empty seat and "B" for a booked seat. The array already contains the bookings for tonight's film. A ticket costs $8.50.
tasks: count and output the number of empty seats in each row, and in the whole cinema
allow a customer to book seats one at a time by inputting a row number and a seat number, with validation that each is in range
book the chosen seat if it is empty, otherwise output a message to say that it is already taken
keep booking until the customer enters 0 for the row number
output how many seats the customer booked and the total cost
req: Nested loops visit every seat in the 2D array (rows 1 to 10, seats 1 to 20)
Counts the empty seats in each row (counter reset for each row) and outputs each row's count
Totals the empty seats for the whole cinema and outputs the total
Inputs the row number and seat number with suitable prompts
Validates the row (0 to 10) and the seat (1 to 20) with a loop that asks again
Checks whether the chosen seat holds "E" before booking it
Sets the seat to "B" when it is booked, or outputs a message if it is taken
Repeats the booking until 0 is entered for the row number
Counts the seats booked and outputs the number and the total cost at $8.50 each
pc_cinema.model:
// Count and output the empty seats in each row and in the whole cinema
TotalEmpty ← 0
FOR Row ← 1 TO 10
    RowEmpty ← 0
    FOR Seat ← 1 TO 20
        IF Seats[Row, Seat] = "E"
          THEN
            RowEmpty ← RowEmpty + 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Seat
    OUTPUT "Row ", Row, " has ", RowEmpty, " empty seats"
    TotalEmpty ← TotalEmpty + RowEmpty
NEXT Row
OUTPUT "Empty seats in the cinema: ", TotalEmpty

// Let the customer book seats one at a time
Booked ← 0
REPEAT
    // Input the row number and check it is from 0 to 10
    OUTPUT "Enter the row number (1 to 10), or 0 to finish"
    INPUT Row
    WHILE Row < 0 OR Row > 10 DO
        OUTPUT "Invalid row. Enter a number from 0 to 10"
        INPUT Row
    ENDWHILE
    IF Row <> 0
      THEN
        // Input the seat number and check it is from 1 to 20
        OUTPUT "Enter the seat number (1 to 20)"
        INPUT Seat
        WHILE Seat < 1 OR Seat > 20 DO
            OUTPUT "Invalid seat. Enter a number from 1 to 20"
            INPUT Seat
        ENDWHILE
        // Only book the seat if it is empty
        IF Seats[Row, Seat] = "E"
          THEN
            Seats[Row, Seat] ← "B"
            Booked ← Booked + 1
            OUTPUT "Row ", Row, " seat ", Seat, " is now booked for you"
          ELSE
            OUTPUT "Sorry, that seat is already taken"
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
UNTIL Row = 0

// Output the number of seats booked and the total cost
Cost ← Booked * 8.5
OUTPUT "You booked ", Booked, " seats"
OUTPUT "Total cost: $", Cost

pc_quiz.title: Class quiz results
pc_quiz.intro: A teacher sets 5 quizzes during a term for a class of 30 students. The array StudentName[1:30] stores the students' names. The 2D array QuizScore[1:30, 1:5] stores each student's score out of 20 for each quiz. Both arrays already contain data, except for quiz 5, which the class took late. The array AverageScore[1:30] will store each student's average score.
tasks: input the quiz 5 score for every student, with validation that it is from 0 to 20, and store it in QuizScore
calculate each student's average score over the 5 quizzes, rounded to one decimal place, and store it in AverageScore
give each student a grade: an average of 15 or more is "Distinction", 10 or more is "Merit", otherwise "Pass"
output each student's name, average and grade
output how many students got each grade
output the name and average of the student with the highest average
req: Loops through all 30 students to input the quiz 5 score, with a prompt
Validates each score (0 to 20) with a loop that asks again, and stores it in QuizScore[Student, 5]
A nested loop totals the 5 quiz scores for each student, with the total reset for each student
Calculates the average (total ÷ 5), rounded to 1 decimal place, and stores it in AverageScore
Selection gives the correct grade (15 or more Distinction, 10 or more Merit, otherwise Pass)
Outputs each student's name, average and grade
Counts each grade, with the counters set to 0 first, and outputs the three counts
Finds the highest average and remembers which student it belongs to
Outputs the name and average of the student with the highest average
pc_quiz.model:
// Set the grade counters to zero
DistinctionCount ← 0
MeritCount ← 0
PassCount ← 0

// Input the late quiz 5 score for every student
FOR Student ← 1 TO 30
    OUTPUT "Enter the quiz 5 score for ", StudentName[Student]
    INPUT Score
    // The score must be from 0 to 20
    WHILE Score < 0 OR Score > 20 DO
        OUTPUT "Invalid score. Enter a score from 0 to 20"
        INPUT Score
    ENDWHILE
    QuizScore[Student, 5] ← Score
NEXT Student

// Work out each student's average and grade
HighestAverage ← -1
HighestName ← ""
FOR Student ← 1 TO 30
    Total ← 0
    FOR Quiz ← 1 TO 5
        Total ← Total + QuizScore[Student, Quiz]
    NEXT Quiz
    AverageScore[Student] ← ROUND(Total / 5, 1)
    // Decide the grade from the average
    IF AverageScore[Student] >= 15
      THEN
        Grade ← "Distinction"
        DistinctionCount ← DistinctionCount + 1
      ELSE
        IF AverageScore[Student] >= 10
          THEN
            Grade ← "Merit"
            MeritCount ← MeritCount + 1
          ELSE
            Grade ← "Pass"
            PassCount ← PassCount + 1
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    OUTPUT StudentName[Student], " average: ", AverageScore[Student], " grade: ", Grade
    // Remember the highest average so far
    IF AverageScore[Student] > HighestAverage
      THEN
        HighestAverage ← AverageScore[Student]
        HighestName ← StudentName[Student]
    ENDIF
NEXT Student

// Output the grade counts and the top student
OUTPUT "Distinctions: ", DistinctionCount
OUTPUT "Merits: ", MeritCount
OUTPUT "Passes: ", PassCount
OUTPUT "Highest average: ", HighestName, " with ", HighestAverage

pc_gym.title: Gym member log-in
pc_gym.intro: A gym has 200 members. Each member has a member number and a 4-digit PIN. The array MemberNumber[1:200] stores the member numbers, MemberPIN[1:200] stores each member's PIN and Visits[1:200] stores how many times each member has visited this month. The data at the same index in each array belongs to the same member. The arrays already contain the data.
tasks: show a menu with three options: 1 log in, 2 show the member with the most visits, 3 exit, with validation of the choice
option 1: input a member number and search for it, outputting a message if it is not found
if the member is found, allow up to 3 attempts to enter the correct PIN
after a correct PIN, add 1 to the member's visits and output a welcome message with their number of visits this month; after 3 wrong attempts output "Account locked, please see reception"
option 2: output the member number and visits of the member with the most visits
keep showing the menu until option 3 is chosen
req: Outputs a menu with the three options and repeats it until option 3 is chosen
Validates the menu choice (1 to 3) with a loop that asks again
Uses selection (CASE or IF) to run the chosen option
Inputs a member number and does a linear search of MemberNumber
Outputs a suitable message if the member number is not found
A loop allows up to 3 PIN attempts, comparing with MemberPIN at the same index
After a correct PIN, adds 1 to Visits at that index and outputs a welcome message with the visits
After 3 wrong attempts, outputs the locked message
Finds the member with the most visits and outputs their member number and visits
pc_gym.model:
REPEAT
    // Show the menu and validate the choice
    OUTPUT "1 Log in   2 Most visits   3 Exit"
    OUTPUT "Enter your choice (1, 2 or 3)"
    INPUT Choice
    WHILE Choice < 1 OR Choice > 3 DO
        OUTPUT "Invalid choice. Enter 1, 2 or 3"
        INPUT Choice
    ENDWHILE
    CASE OF Choice
        1 : // Log in: linear search for the member number
            OUTPUT "Enter your member number"
            INPUT SearchNumber
            Index ← 0
            Found ← FALSE
            WHILE Found = FALSE AND Index < 200 DO
                Index ← Index + 1
                IF MemberNumber[Index] = SearchNumber
                  THEN
                    Found ← TRUE
                ENDIF
            ENDWHILE
            IF Found = FALSE
              THEN
                OUTPUT "Member number not found"
              ELSE
                // Allow up to 3 attempts at the PIN
                Attempts ← 0
                Correct ← FALSE
                REPEAT
                    OUTPUT "Enter your PIN"
                    INPUT EnteredPIN
                    Attempts ← Attempts + 1
                    IF EnteredPIN = MemberPIN[Index]
                      THEN
                        Correct ← TRUE
                      ELSE
                        OUTPUT "Incorrect PIN"
                    ENDIF
                UNTIL Correct = TRUE OR Attempts = 3
                IF Correct = TRUE
                  THEN
                    // Record the visit and welcome the member
                    Visits[Index] ← Visits[Index] + 1
                    OUTPUT "Welcome! This is visit ", Visits[Index], " this month"
                  ELSE
                    OUTPUT "Account locked, please see reception"
                ENDIF
            ENDIF
        2 : // Find the member with the most visits
            MostIndex ← 1
            FOR Count ← 2 TO 200
                IF Visits[Count] > Visits[MostIndex]
                  THEN
                    MostIndex ← Count
                ENDIF
            NEXT Count
            OUTPUT "Member ", MemberNumber[MostIndex], " has the most visits: ", Visits[MostIndex]
        3 : OUTPUT "Goodbye"
    ENDCASE
UNTIL Choice = 3

pc_weather.title: Weather station
pc_weather.intro: A weather station records the temperature every hour for one week. The 2D array Temp[1:7, 1:24] stores the temperatures in °C as real numbers, with one row for each day and one column for each hour. The array DayName[1:7] stores the names of the days, from "Monday" to "Sunday". Both arrays already contain the data.
tasks: for each day, find the highest temperature, the lowest temperature and the average temperature to one decimal place, and output them with the day name
output the name of the day with the biggest difference between its highest and lowest temperature
count and output how many readings in the whole week were above 30 °C
allow the user to input a day name, with validation that it is one of the days in DayName, then output all 24 readings for that day with the hour number
req: Nested loops go through all 7 days and all 24 hours
Highest and lowest start from a reading (not 0) for each day and are updated by comparison
The total is reset for each day and the average (total ÷ 24) is rounded to 1 decimal place
Outputs each day's name with its highest, lowest and average temperature
Works out each day's difference (highest − lowest) and keeps the biggest one with its day
Outputs the name of the day with the biggest difference
Counts the readings above 30 °C across the whole week and outputs the count
Inputs a day name and validates it against DayName, asking again if it is not found
Outputs all 24 readings for the chosen day with the hour number
pc_weather.model:
BiggestRange ← -1
BiggestDay ← ""
HotCount ← 0
FOR Day ← 1 TO 7
    // Start the highest and lowest with the first reading of the day
    Highest ← Temp[Day, 1]
    Lowest ← Temp[Day, 1]
    Total ← 0
    FOR Hour ← 1 TO 24
        Reading ← Temp[Day, Hour]
        Total ← Total + Reading
        IF Reading > Highest
          THEN
            Highest ← Reading
        ENDIF
        IF Reading < Lowest
          THEN
            Lowest ← Reading
        ENDIF
        // Count the readings above 30 degrees
        IF Reading > 30
          THEN
            HotCount ← HotCount + 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Hour
    Average ← ROUND(Total / 24, 1)
    OUTPUT DayName[Day], ": highest ", Highest, ", lowest ", Lowest, ", average ", Average
    // Remember the day with the biggest difference
    IF Highest - Lowest > BiggestRange
      THEN
        BiggestRange ← Highest - Lowest
        BiggestDay ← DayName[Day]
    ENDIF
NEXT Day
OUTPUT "The biggest difference was on ", BiggestDay, ": ", BiggestRange, " degrees"
OUTPUT "Readings above 30 degrees: ", HotCount

// Input a day name and check it is one of the days in DayName
DayNumber ← 0
WHILE DayNumber = 0 DO
    OUTPUT "Enter a day name, for example Monday"
    INPUT Choice
    FOR Day ← 1 TO 7
        IF DayName[Day] = Choice
          THEN
            DayNumber ← Day
        ENDIF
    NEXT Day
    IF DayNumber = 0
      THEN
        OUTPUT "That is not a valid day name"
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE
// Output every reading for that day with its hour
FOR Hour ← 1 TO 24
    OUTPUT "Hour ", Hour, ": ", Temp[DayNumber, Hour], " degrees"
NEXT Hour

pc_shop.title: Tuck shop orders
pc_shop.intro: A school tuck shop sells 50 different items. The array ItemName[1:50] stores the name of each item, ItemPrice[1:50] stores the price of each item and Stock[1:50] stores how many of each item are in stock. The data at the same index in each array belongs to the same item. The arrays already contain the data.
tasks: allow a student to order items: input an item name and search for it, outputting a message if it is not found
if the item is found, output a message if it is out of stock; otherwise input the quantity wanted, with validation that it is at least 1 and no more than the number in stock
reduce the stock and add the cost to a running total for the order
keep taking items until the student enters "END", then output the total cost of the order
then sort the three arrays into ascending order of stock using a bubble sort, keeping each item's name, price and stock together
output the name and stock of every item with fewer than 5 left, lowest stock first
req: Inputs item names in a loop that stops when "END" is entered
Linear search of ItemName, with a message if the item is not found
Checks whether the item is out of stock before asking for a quantity
Validates the quantity (at least 1 and no more than the stock) with a loop that asks again
Reduces the stock at the same index by the quantity ordered
Running total of quantity × price, set to 0 first and output when the order ends
Bubble sort into ascending order of stock, comparing adjacent elements and repeating passes
Swaps the name, price and stock together using temporary variables
Outputs the name and stock of each item with fewer than 5 left, in order
pc_shop.model:
// Take the order until the student enters END
OrderTotal ← 0
OUTPUT "Enter an item name, or END to finish"
INPUT WantedItem
WHILE WantedItem <> "END" DO
    // Linear search for the item
    Found ← FALSE
    Index ← 1
    WHILE Found = FALSE AND Index <= 50 DO
        IF ItemName[Index] = WantedItem
          THEN
            Found ← TRUE
          ELSE
            Index ← Index + 1
        ENDIF
    ENDWHILE
    IF Found = FALSE
      THEN
        OUTPUT "Sorry, we do not sell ", WantedItem
      ELSE
        IF Stock[Index] = 0
          THEN
            OUTPUT "Sorry, ", WantedItem, " is out of stock"
          ELSE
            // Input and validate the quantity
            OUTPUT "How many do you want? (1 to ", Stock[Index], ")"
            INPUT Quantity
            WHILE Quantity < 1 OR Quantity > Stock[Index] DO
                OUTPUT "Please enter a number from 1 to ", Stock[Index]
                INPUT Quantity
            ENDWHILE
            // Update the stock and the running total
            Stock[Index] ← Stock[Index] - Quantity
            OrderTotal ← OrderTotal + Quantity * ItemPrice[Index]
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    OUTPUT "Enter an item name, or END to finish"
    INPUT WantedItem
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT "Total cost of your order: $", OrderTotal

// Bubble sort all three arrays into ascending order of stock
Top ← 49
REPEAT
    Swapped ← FALSE
    FOR Count ← 1 TO Top
        IF Stock[Count] > Stock[Count + 1]
          THEN
            // Swap stock, name and price so each item stays together
            TempStock ← Stock[Count]
            Stock[Count] ← Stock[Count + 1]
            Stock[Count + 1] ← TempStock
            TempName ← ItemName[Count]
            ItemName[Count] ← ItemName[Count + 1]
            ItemName[Count + 1] ← TempName
            TempPrice ← ItemPrice[Count]
            ItemPrice[Count] ← ItemPrice[Count + 1]
            ItemPrice[Count + 1] ← TempPrice
            Swapped ← TRUE
        ENDIF
    NEXT Count
    Top ← Top - 1
UNTIL Swapped = FALSE OR Top = 0

// Output the items to restock, lowest stock first
OUTPUT "Items to restock:"
FOR Count ← 1 TO 50
    IF Stock[Count] < 5
      THEN
        OUTPUT ItemName[Count], ": ", Stock[Count], " left"
    ENDIF
NEXT Count

pc_race.title: Sports day race
pc_race.intro: Eight runners take part in the final of the 200 m race at sports day. The array Runner[1:8] stores the runners' names and already contains the data. The array RaceTime[1:8] will store each runner's time in seconds. The variable SchoolRecord already stores the current school record time in seconds.
tasks: input the time for each runner and store it in RaceTime; a time must be more than 20 seconds and less than 60 seconds
sort the runners into finishing order, fastest first, using a bubble sort, so that each runner's name stays with their time
output each runner's position, name and time, adding "Gold", "Silver" or "Bronze" for the first three
output the average time for the race, rounded to 2 decimal places
if the winner beat the school record, output a message and update SchoolRecord
req: A loop inputs a time for each of the 8 runners, with a prompt that names the runner
Validates each time (more than 20 and less than 60) with a loop that asks again
Bubble sort compares adjacent times and repeats until no swaps are made (or enough passes)
Swaps both the time and the name using temporary variables
Outputs the position, name and time of every runner, fastest first
Adds Gold, Silver and Bronze for positions 1 to 3 only
Totals the times and outputs the average rounded to 2 decimal places
Compares the winner's time with SchoolRecord
Outputs a record message and updates SchoolRecord when it is beaten
pc_race.model:
// Input and validate each runner's time
FOR Count ← 1 TO 8
    OUTPUT "Enter the time in seconds for ", Runner[Count]
    INPUT RaceTime[Count]
    WHILE RaceTime[Count] <= 20 OR RaceTime[Count] >= 60 DO
        OUTPUT "The time must be more than 20 and less than 60. Enter it again"
        INPUT RaceTime[Count]
    ENDWHILE
NEXT Count

// Bubble sort the times into ascending order, moving the names with them
REPEAT
    Swapped ← FALSE
    FOR Count ← 1 TO 7
        IF RaceTime[Count] > RaceTime[Count + 1]
          THEN
            TempTime ← RaceTime[Count]
            RaceTime[Count] ← RaceTime[Count + 1]
            RaceTime[Count + 1] ← TempTime
            TempName ← Runner[Count]
            Runner[Count] ← Runner[Count + 1]
            Runner[Count + 1] ← TempName
            Swapped ← TRUE
        ENDIF
    NEXT Count
UNTIL Swapped = FALSE

// Output the results with medals and total the times
Total ← 0
FOR Position ← 1 TO 8
    Total ← Total + RaceTime[Position]
    CASE OF Position
        1 : Medal ← " Gold"
        2 : Medal ← " Silver"
        3 : Medal ← " Bronze"
        OTHERWISE : Medal ← ""
    ENDCASE
    OUTPUT Position, ". ", Runner[Position], " ", RaceTime[Position], " seconds", Medal
NEXT Position
OUTPUT "Average time: ", ROUND(Total / 8, 2), " seconds"

// Check whether the winner broke the school record
IF RaceTime[1] < SchoolRecord
  THEN
    OUTPUT "New school record by ", Runner[1], "!"
    SchoolRecord ← RaceTime[1]
ENDIF
